speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you describe how long you've had these symptoms and if they are itchy, painful, or oozing?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (cradle cap) with possible atopic dermatitis superinfection or misdiagnosed psoriasis given the family history; however, the "cold weather" exacerbation and "red/scaly" description in a 3-month-old is most consistent with Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis. No further testing is required at this stage.
